title: Rail-to-Rail Input Amplifiers
text:
2 Introduction
The input stage of op-amp may need to tolerate rail-to-rail swing in case of unity feedback configuration under a common mode that swings rail to rail [1]. Usually, there is only a single input pair and the input is directly fed to the gates of this pair. Rail-to-Rail input swing in unity configuration requires one of the following choices:

Use of complementary input pairs - a PMOS and an NMOS input pair
Shifting the common-mode of the input fed to a single input pair

The first consideration is supply voltage, for supplies below ~1.2V, the use of complementary input pairs becomes infeasible. Next, the choice of whether to keep the input pair in strong or weak-inversion affects the gm-variation across input variation. Once these two constraints are settled, various creative topologies can be employed competing against each other on following specs:

CMRR
THD
Slew Rate
Power burnt
UGB variation across input variation

The fundamental relations to be kepy in mind are:

In Weak inversion, \[
\frac{g_m}{I_D} = \text{Constant}
\]
In Strong Inversion, \[
g_m = \sqrt{2\beta I_D} = \frac{2I_D}{V_{ov}}
\]

title: Rail-to-Rail Input Amplifiers
text:
3 Weak Inversion Theory

3.1 Drain Current Expression
In weak inversion, the drain current can be approximated as
\[
I_D = I_0 \exp\left(\frac{V_{GS} - V_{TH}}{n U_T}\right)
\]
where \(U_T = kT/q\) is the thermal voltage and \(n\) is the subthreshold slope factor [2].


3.2 Transconductance Efficiency
The transconductance-to-current ratio is
\[
\frac{g_m}{I_D} = \frac{1}{n U_T}
\]
which is maximized in weak inversion, making it attractive for low-power amplifiers [3].

title: Rail-to-Rail Input Amplifiers
text:
4 Circuit Implications

4.1 Current Mirrors
Weak inversion current mirrors provide excellent matching at low currents, though they are sensitive to temperature and process variation.


4.2 Low-Voltage Biasing
Because \(V_{GS}\) is close to \(V_{TH}\), circuits can operate with supplies below 1 V [4].

title: Rail-to-Rail Input Amplifiers
text:
5 Limitations
Despite its advantages, weak inversion design suffers from: - reduced bandwidth - increased noise - strong temperature dependence
These trade-offs must be carefully evaluated.

title: Rail-to-Rail Input Amplifiers
text:
6 Conclusion
Weak inversion remains a powerful technique for ultra-low-power analog systems, particularly in biomedical and IoT applications. Proper modeling and careful biasing are essential for robust operation.

text:
3 Methodology
We have studied a collection of literature reviews on such techniques and have selected few canonical or exotic topologies for simulation in proprietary pdk for our understanding. We have also replicated our learnings on open-source skywater 130nm pdk simulated on colab. You can access details of each topology via the left sidebar. All the colab notebooks are accessible on our github and are simulatable on a single click. We look forward to collaboration and feedback on future extension of this work
